source.title: New optimization algorithms for neural network training using operator splitting techniques
source.authors: C. Alecsa; Titus Pinta; Imre Boros

record.file_problem: The supplied full text is readable, though some figure labels are garbled. Relevant accuracy values are available in tables.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizers on image classifiers and reports training and test accuracy, using its own training setup rather than reproducing the referenced optimizer studies.
record.gate_note: The optimizer comparisons are the study’s own results. The cited claims about SGD and Nesterov generalizing better than adaptive methods are prior work, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons on image classifiers. Tables 1–2 and Figure 4 bear on V4, although the comparisons use limited learning-rate choices, fixed epoch budgets and one initialization.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately captures the authors' stated conclusion: their splitting methods are competitive with momentum methods and empirically generalize better than adaptive methods. However, that conclusion is associated with Figure 4 and the discussion; Tables 1–2 include settings where Adam beats SGD or Nesterov, so it should not be presented as a uniform result across their experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces and evaluates operator-splitting optimizers; it does not reproduce the original optimizer-comparison protocols. It uses single-seed image-classifier experiments and reports train/test accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, learning rate, epoch count, optimizer, and random initialization affect the reported outcomes. The authors state that results depend heavily on randomized weights and biases and that the splitting methods’ k parameter needs tuning.
record.problems: The authors state that they used a fixed random seed and that results depend heavily on weight and bias initialization; they call for multiple simulations to obtain average test accuracy. No uncertainty estimates are reported for accuracy results.
record.rows_left_out: Accuracy values for additional epoch, learning-rate, and optimizer conditions in Tables 1–2 were omitted to keep the extraction focused on the Adam, SGD, and Nesterov comparison for V4. Figure-only trajectories and training-time tables do not directly add results for this version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, systematic broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions; merely omitting dropout is not a comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.

missing.what: Figure 4's adaptive versus SGD/Nesterov comparison directly bears on V4, contrary to the record's dismissal of figure trajectories. Record the explicitly stated direction and settings; mark exact values unreadable. Adam and RMSprop use 0.003, SGD and Nesterov use 0.5, Nesterov momentum is 0.5, and training lasts 150 epochs.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded accuracy values and table orientations agree with the supplied text. Optimizer names identify training methods rather than model architectures. No accuracy uncertainty estimates or repeated-seed averages are supplied. The record's E2 misattributes a sentence about RMSprop to Adam. Proposed-method performance alone should not substitute for the SGD/Nesterov comparisons named by V4.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; optimizer comparisons beyond the tested image classifiers and settings.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to batch size.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: MNIST, 100 epochs, SGD and Adam both at learning rate 0.001
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show Adam test accuracy 0.9907 versus SGD's 0.9886, reversing the proposed disadvantage in this setting; this does not refute an across-benchmark tendency.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly achieved test accuracy 0.9907 versus SGD's 0.9886, but this shared-learning-rate comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: MNIST, 50 epochs, Nesterov at learning rate 0.1 versus Adam at 0.001
relationships.reason: R7 reaches 0.9942; the same-budget Adam result in Table 1 is 0.9909. The Adam comparator is taken from the text's table and was explicitly omitted from the record.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy favored Nesterov over Adam at the same epoch budget, but the comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Fashion-MNIST, recorded SGD and Nesterov comparisons with Adam
relationships.reason: R3–R4 show Adam beating SGD at 100 epochs, 0.9081 versus 0.8821; R8 also trails the table's same-budget Adam result at 50 epochs, 0.8874 versus 0.9063.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly exceeded SGD and Nesterov at their respective matched training budgets, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R5–R6 and R9 show Adam test accuracy 0.9254 exceeding both SGD's 0.8313 and Nesterov's 0.9108.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly achieved test accuracy 0.9254 versus SGD's 0.8313 and Nesterov's 0.9108, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, Figure 4 alternative learning-rate and momentum settings
relationships.reason: Based on Remark 9 and the discussion, rather than recorded rows: the authors explicitly report better generalization for non-adaptive methods in this experiment. Exact figure values are unreadable in the supplied text.
relationships.display_finding: Nonadaptive methods reportedly generalized better under the alternative settings, but exact values were unreadable and the comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The three image-classification datasets and optimizer settings represented in R1–R9
reader_labels.reason: Adam and SGD test accuracies vary by dataset and setting; Adam exceeds SGD on CIFAR-10 at 150 epochs, while the reported MNIST and MNIST-Fashion outcomes do not establish a consistent adaptive-optimizer disadvantage (R1–R6). The paper also reports Nesterov comparisons (R7–R9).
